name: statfd
description: stat(2) and fstat(2) must give the SAME answer for the same object (apple/fgx#366).  /testbin/statid stats `/' by NAME and fstats it by DESCRIPTOR and prints MATCH or MISMATCH, rather than leaving a fixture to match printed numbers with exact spacing -- a program that only prints cannot fail.  GOES RED WITHOUT THE FIX, and that is measured rather than assumed: forcing `_Sys_Fstat' back down the legacy arm (`CLC' in place of the `JSR _Fs_RootFstat') takes this to `missing SID MATCH' + `unexpectedly contains SID MISMATCH'.  Before the fix `_Sys_Fstat' answered from the FCB, which cannot know an inode, so fstat reported st_ino 0 where stat reported the real 2; libc's stat.c wrote that up as intended behaviour and no caller could tell a `not reported' zero from a real one.  THE getwd ARM IS A SMOKE ASSERTION AND NOT A DISCRIMINATOR, and it is labelled so because it was nearly shipped as the opposite: the same mutation run leaves `SID getwd=[/root]' PASSING.  getwd walks up until fstat's inode equals stat's, and with both broken values reading 0 it exits through its second break (`cino == d.st_ino', 0 == 0) one iteration late with the right answer by accident.  It is kept because it proves getwd runs and returns at all, which nothing else here does -- not because it witnesses this fix.  MATCH is a `contains' and MISMATCH only a `lacks': a run that never reached the program prints neither word, and a `lacks' alone passes when nothing ran.
